purpose: Set rules for any future public rendering of sensory/material-room records.
required_tests_before_publication: Does the sensory detail orient or protect the reader, rather than merely making the scene vivid?
Could this object, smell, sound, photograph, room layout, medication, or timing identify a person or family?
Does the language preserve dignity of the dead person, the family, and the worker?
Does any sentence imply diagnosis, prediction, procedure, therapy, ritual, legal duty, or facility policy?
Would the page still be accurate if the detail were replaced with a less vivid phrase? If yes, use the less vivid phrase.
Has the relevant high-gate review been completed for child, suicide, custody, disaster, tradition, body-work, or official scenes?
recommended_public_shape: what public sources can safely say
when to route to care team/local authority/tradition holder
